questions.question:
The `frontend-zone` namespace runs the deployment `storefront` (label `app=storefront`) which serves on port `80` and pulls its image from the internal registry as `registry.localhost:5000/ckx/nginx:v1.25`. Right now every pod in the cluster can reach it. Lock the namespace down:

1. Apply a default-deny ingress policy named `default-deny-ingress` in `frontend-zone` that selects all pods and denies all ingress.
2. Apply a second NetworkPolicy named `allow-trusted-clients` that allows ingress to pods with label `app=storefront` on TCP port `80` ONLY from pods in namespaces carrying the label `tier=trusted` (the namespace `trusted-clients` already has this label and runs a `client` pod).

The trusted client must be able to reach `storefront` on port 80; pods in the namespace `untrusted-clients` must be blocked.

verification.description: default-deny-ingress policy selects all pods and denies all ingress
allow-trusted-clients policy selects app=storefront and admits port 80 only from tier=trusted namespaces
trusted-clients pod can reach storefront on TCP 80 with both policies in place (allowed path works)
allow-trusted-clients admits ingress only from tier=trusted namespaces (untrusted denied by policy)

questions.question:
The `gateway-edge` namespace exposes the deployment `portal` (label `app=portal`, image `registry.localhost:5000/ckx/nginx:v1.25`) through the Service `portal-svc` on port `80`. External traffic must be served over TLS only.

1. Create a TLS Secret named `portal-tls` of type `kubernetes.io/tls` in `gateway-edge`. A self-signed certificate and key for host `portal.ckx.local` are already provided at `/tmp/exam/q2/tls.crt` and `/tmp/exam/q2/tls.key`.
2. Create an Ingress named `portal-ingress` in `gateway-edge` that routes host `portal.ckx.local` (path `/`, `pathType: Prefix`) to `portal-svc` on port `80`, and terminates TLS for host `portal.ckx.local` using the `portal-tls` secret.

The backend `portal` deployment must be Running from the internal registry image.

verification.description: portal-tls secret exists, is type kubernetes.io/tls, and carries the provided cert/key
portal-ingress routes host portal.ckx.local path / (Prefix) to portal-svc:80
portal-ingress terminates TLS for portal.ckx.local using the portal-tls secret

questions.question:
A security review of the `audit-team` namespace found that the ServiceAccount `report-sa` is bound, through the RoleBinding `report-sa-binding`, to a Role named `report-role` that grants `verbs: ["*"]` on `resources: ["*"]`. Apply least privilege:

Reshape `report-role` so that `report-sa` can only `get`, `list`, and `watch` `configmaps` in `audit-team` and nothing else. Keep the RoleBinding pointing the same ServiceAccount at the same Role.

After your change, `report-sa` must still be able to `list configmaps`, but must NOT be able to `delete pods` in `audit-team`.

verification.description: report-sa can get configmaps but can NOT get secrets in audit-team (scoped allow)
report-sa cannot delete pods in audit-team (privilege removed)
report-role rules are scoped to configmaps get/list/watch only (no wildcards)

questions.question:
On-call engineers in the `support-rbac` namespace use the ServiceAccount `oncall-sa`. They must be able to read pods and pod logs for debugging, but the security team requires that they can NOT open shells in containers. The Role `oncall-role` and its RoleBinding `oncall-binding` already exist but are misconfigured.

Configure `oncall-role` so that `oncall-sa` can `get`, `list`, and `watch` `pods` and `get` `pods/log`, but is denied `create` on `pods/exec`.

After your change, `oncall-sa` must be able to `get pods/log`, but must NOT be able to `create pods/exec` in `support-rbac`.

verification.description: oncall-sa can get pods and pods/log but can no longer create pods in support-rbac
oncall-sa cannot create pods/exec in support-rbac (exec denied)
oncall-role grants only pods get/list/watch and pods/log get

questions.question:
The cluster must only run images served by the internal registry. The namespace `registry-guard` is labelled `registry-policy=enforced`.

Using a `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` (CEL-based, built into the cluster):

1. Create a `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` named `trusted-registry-only` that, for `CREATE`/`UPDATE` of `pods`, requires every container image to start with the prefix `registry.localhost:5000/`.
2. Bind it with a `ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding` named `trusted-registry-only-binding` whose `matchResources` targets namespaces with label `registry-policy=enforced`, with `validationActions: [Deny]`.

A pod that references a public image such as `nginx:1.25` must be rejected in `registry-guard`; a pod that uses `registry.localhost:5000/ckx/nginx:v1.25` must be admitted.

verification.description: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and binding exist and target the registry-policy=enforced namespace with Deny
a pod using a non-registry image is rejected in registry-guard (violation captured)
a pod using registry.localhost:5000/ckx/nginx:v1.25 is admitted in registry-guard

questions.question:
The deployment `edge-cache` in the `system-lockdown` namespace runs the internal-registry image `registry.localhost:5000/ckx/alpine:3.20` (command `sleep infinity`) but was created by a contractor with an over-permissive container: it adds the `SYS_ADMIN` and `NET_RAW` capabilities and allows privilege escalation. Harden the container security context so that the pod keeps running:

1. Drop ALL capabilities (`capabilities.drop: ["ALL"]`) and add none back.
2. Set `runAsNonRoot: true` and `runAsUser: 10001`.
3. Set `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` and `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`.

The `edge-cache` pod must end up Running from the internal registry image with the hardened context applied.

verification.description: edge-cache container drops ALL capabilities, runs as non-root user 10001, no privilege escalation, read-only rootfs
edge-cache pod is Running from registry.localhost:5000/ckx/alpine:3.20

questions.question:
The deployment `metrics-shipper` in the `syscall-lockdown` namespace runs `registry.localhost:5000/ckx/alpine:3.20` (command `sleep infinity`) but explicitly sets its seccomp profile to `Unconfined`, leaving every syscall open. Restore syscall filtering:

Set the pod-level seccomp profile to `RuntimeDefault` (`spec.securityContext.seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault`) and remove the `Unconfined` setting.

The `metrics-shipper` pod must be Running from the internal registry image with the `RuntimeDefault` seccomp profile applied.

verification.description: metrics-shipper uses seccompProfile type RuntimeDefault (Unconfined removed)
metrics-shipper pod is Running from registry.localhost:5000/ckx/alpine:3.20

questions.question:
The `microsvc-restricted` namespace must be brought up to the `restricted` Pod Security Standard. It currently runs the deployment `orders-ui` (image `registry.localhost:5000/ckx/alpine:3.20`, command `sleep infinity`) which is NOT compliant.

1. Label the namespace to `enforce` the `restricted` standard at the current version, and also set `warn` and `audit` to `restricted`.
2. Patch `orders-ui` so it satisfies the restricted policy: `runAsNonRoot: true`, `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, `capabilities.drop: ["ALL"]`, and `seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault`. Use `runAsUser: 10001`.

The `orders-ui` pod must be Running. A pod that violates the restricted policy (for example a privileged pod) must be rejected by the namespace.

verification.description: namespace enforces restricted PSA and sets warn/audit to restricted
orders-ui pod is compliant and Running from the internal registry image
a privileged pod is rejected by the restricted namespace (violation captured)
warn and audit modes are both set to restricted

questions.question:
The deployment `billing` in the `payments-svc` namespace injects a database password directly as a plaintext environment variable (`DB_PASSWORD: S3cr3t-P@ss!`) in its pod spec, and it automounts the default ServiceAccount token even though it never calls the API. Fix the credential hygiene:

1. Create a Secret named `billing-db` in `payments-svc` with key `password` set to `S3cr3t-P@ss!`.
2. Update `billing` so the container reads `DB_PASSWORD` from the `billing-db` secret (via `secretKeyRef`) instead of a plaintext value. No plaintext password may remain in the pod spec.
3. Set `automountServiceAccountToken: false` for the `billing` pod.

The `billing` pod must be Running from `registry.localhost:5000/ckx/nginx:v1.25`.

verification.description: billing-db secret exists with password=S3cr3t-P@ss!
billing reads DB_PASSWORD via secretKeyRef and has no plaintext password in the pod spec
billing pod disables ServiceAccount token automount and is Running from the registry image

questions.question:
The deployment `processor` (label `app=processor`, image `registry.localhost:5000/ckx/alpine:3.20`, command `sleep infinity`) in the `txn-mesh` namespace currently has unrestricted egress. Apply zero-trust egress:

1. Create a NetworkPolicy named `processor-egress` that selects pods with label `app=processor` and denies all egress except:
   - DNS resolution (UDP and TCP port `53` to any destination), and
   - TCP port `80` to pods in the namespace labelled `tier=ledger` (the namespace `txn-ledger` already carries this label and runs the service `ledger-svc`).

After your change, `processor` must be able to reach `ledger-svc.txn-ledger` on port 80, but egress to any other namespace (for example the `ledger-svc` equivalent in `txn-public`) must be blocked.

verification.description: processor-egress policy exists, selects app=processor, and is an Egress policy that permits DNS
processor can reach ledger-svc.txn-ledger on TCP 80 (allowed egress works)
processor-egress scopes port-80 egress to tier=ledger only (txn-public denied by policy)

questions.question:
The deployment `web-frontend` in the `supply-frontend` namespace references its image by the MUTABLE tag `registry.localhost:5000/ckx/nginx:v1.25`. Supply-chain policy requires immutable digest pinning.

1. Determine the current manifest digest of `ckx/nginx:v1.25` in the internal registry. (From the jumphost you can query the registry HTTP API, for example: `curl -sI -H 'Accept: application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json' http://registry:5000/v2/ckx/nginx/manifests/v1.25 | grep -i docker-content-digest`.)
2. Update `web-frontend` so the container image is pinned by digest as `registry.localhost:5000/ckx/nginx@sha256:<digest>`.

The `web-frontend` pod must be Running using the digest-pinned reference, and the digest must match the registry's current digest for that tag.

verification.description: web-frontend image is pinned by @sha256 digest (no mutable tag)
the pinned digest matches the registry's current digest for ckx/nginx:v1.25
web-frontend pod is Running with the digest-pinned image

questions.question:
A third-party Kubernetes manifest was delivered to `/tmp/exam/q12/workload.yaml`. It defines a Deployment that runs privileged, allows privilege escalation, and runs as root. Use the jumphost `trivy` tool (offline config scanning, no database download needed) to find the misconfigurations, then deploy a hardened version:

1. Run `trivy config /tmp/exam/q12/workload.yaml` and save the full report to `/tmp/exam/q12/findings.txt`. The report must contain the Trivy Kubernetes security check IDs (the `KSV` identifiers) for the privileged container and the missing `runAsNonRoot`/`allowPrivilegeEscalation` settings.
2. Deploy a hardened Deployment named `scanner-api` in the `supply-scan` namespace using image `registry.localhost:5000/ckx/alpine:3.20` (command `sleep infinity`) with a secure context: `privileged` removed, `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, `runAsNonRoot: true` (`runAsUser: 10001`), and `capabilities.drop: ["ALL"]`.

The `scanner-api` pod must be Running from the internal registry image.

verification.description: findings.txt exists and contains the KSV check IDs for the privileged/root misconfigurations
scanner-api deployment is hardened and Running from the internal registry image
scanner-api container security context drops ALL caps, no privilege escalation, runs non-root

questions.question:
Two release manifests were delivered to `/tmp/exam/q13/` together with detached cosign signatures and the releaser's public key:

- `release-good.yaml` with signature `release-good.sig`
- `release-bad.yaml` with signature `release-bad.sig`
- public key `releaser.pub`

One manifest was modified after it was signed. You must also produce a software bill of materials for the base image.

1. Generate an SPDX-JSON SBOM for the internal-registry image `ckx/alpine:3.20` and save it to `/tmp/exam/q13/sbom.json` (the image is available to the jumphost docker daemon as `registry:5000/ckx/alpine:3.20`; `syft docker:registry:5000/ckx/alpine:3.20 -o spdx-json` works offline).
2. Use `cosign verify-blob` with `releaser.pub` (offline, transparency log disabled with `--insecure-ignore-tlog`) to determine which manifest still matches its signature. Write the filename of the authentic manifest (just `release-good.yaml` or `release-bad.yaml`) to `/tmp/exam/q13/verified.txt`.
3. Apply ONLY the authentic manifest. It creates the deployment `trusted-release` in `supply-trust`. The tampered manifest must NOT be deployed.

verification.description: sbom.json is valid SPDX-JSON for ckx/alpine and lists packages
verified.txt names release-good.yaml as the authentic manifest
only the authentic deployment trusted-release exists; the tampered one was not deployed

questions.question:
**ANALYSIS TASK** - An API server audit log extract has been collected at `/tmp/exam/q14/audit.log` (one JSON event per line). A ServiceAccount is suspected of reading Secrets it should not. Investigate the log with `jq` and record your findings.

Write a file `/tmp/exam/q14/findings.txt` containing exactly three lines, in this order:

1. `user=<the user/serviceaccount username that performed `get` requests on `secrets`>`
2. `count=<the total number of audit events where that user performed verb `get` on resource `secrets`>`
3. `namespace=<the namespace those secret reads targeted>`

Use the exact `key=value` format with no extra spaces.

verification.description: findings.txt identifies the correct offending serviceaccount username
findings.txt records the correct namespace of the secret reads
findings.txt records the correct count of get-secrets events for that user

questions.question:
The SOC flagged the deployment `ingest-api` in the `runtime-soc` namespace as compromised. It runs its legitimate main container `api` (image `registry.localhost:5000/ckx/alpine:3.20`, command `sleep infinity`) alongside an injected sidecar named `debug` that runs privileged, and the namespace has no egress restrictions. Contain the workload without deleting the deployment:

1. Remove the malicious `debug` sidecar container entirely from `ingest-api`.
2. Harden the remaining `api` container: `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`, `capabilities.drop: ["ALL"]`.
3. Apply a default-deny-all NetworkPolicy named `soc-default-deny` in `runtime-soc` that selects all pods and denies both ingress and egress.

The `ingest-api` pod (single container, hardened) must be Running from the internal registry image.

verification.description: the privileged debug sidecar is removed from ingest-api (only the api container remains)
the api container is hardened (no privilege escalation, read-only rootfs, all caps dropped)
soc-default-deny denies all ingress and egress for all pods in runtime-soc
ingest-api pod is Running from registry.localhost:5000/ckx/nginx:v1.25

questions.question:
The deployment `log-rotator` in the `runtime-immutable` namespace (image `registry.localhost:5000/ckx/alpine:3.20`) writes to `/var/spool/app` on its container's writable root filesystem. Enforce immutable infrastructure so the root filesystem cannot be modified at runtime while the workload keeps functioning:

1. Set `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` on the `log-rotator` container.
2. Provide a writable `emptyDir` volume named `spool` mounted at `/var/spool/app` so the application can still write there.

The container's command is `sh -c 'while true; do echo tick >> /var/spool/app/out.log; sleep 5; done'`. The `log-rotator` pod must be Running from the internal registry image with a read-only root filesystem and the writable emptyDir mounted.

verification.description: log-rotator container has readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
an emptyDir volume is mounted at /var/spool/app
log-rotator pod is Running from registry.localhost:5000/ckx/alpine:3.20
